name: truenorth_sweep_20hz
description: TrueNorth running a complex recurrent network at 20.07 Hz average firing rate with 128 active synapses per neuron, at 0.8 V, all 4096 cores, real-time 1 kHz tick. The census is one 1-second window, so the published average power in mW equals the priced energy in mJ. This is the HELD-OUT middle point: the profile's constants were regressed on the two endpoints only, so this row is a genuine prediction.

census_sources.cells_physical: merolla2014a S1: 256x256 crossbar per core x 4096 cores
census_sources.axons_physical: merolla2014a S1: 256 axons per core x 4096 cores
census_sources.neurons_used: akopyan2015truenorth Fig.17: the characterization networks use every neuron
census_sources.tiles: merolla2014a p.6: one router per core, 64x64 mesh
census_sources.segment_cores: all 4096 cores are configured for the benchmark network
census_sources.sync_count: TrueNorth's 1 kHz tick is the barrier; no extra chip-wide sync
census_sources.timesteps: 1000 ticks = one second at the 1 kHz tick (merolla2014a p.4)
census_sources.latency_steps: the window is 1 s, so average power = mJ per window
census_sources.synaptic_events: 1,048,576 neurons x firing rate x 128 active synapses/neuron (akopyan2015truenorth Fig.17 caption)
census_sources.macs: one synaptic event is one MAC on an event-driven chip
census_sources.host_macs: a bare-chip characterization: no host ComputeOps
census_sources.host_ops_s: a bare-chip characterization: no host wall

average_power_mw.quote: Total TrueNorth chip power breakdown (@ 0.8 V) for three complex recurrent networks with 128 synapses per neuron average, and three different average firing rates. -- bars printed as 68mW @ 11.58Hz, 71mW @ 20.07Hz, 94mW @ 95.93Hz; this row is 71.0mW @ 20.07Hz
